Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Task b7b5979b: fill 5-frames and cast leftward rays

Use when the input contains one or more 5-colored hollow, angular rectangular frames with two full vertical sides and a bottom edge, and a segmented top edge. The demonstrations show color 0 as background and color 2 as the fill/ray color.

## Rule
For each frame:
1. Identify its local bounding box from the 5-pattern. It has a full left and right vertical edge, full bottom edge, and a partial top edge that includes the left corner and the cell next to it, with a gap before the right vertical edge.
2. Recolor every 0 cell strictly inside that frame's bounding box to 2. This includes the gap in the top row between the partial top segment and right vertical, as well as the hollow cavity. Preserve all 5 cells.
3. On the row immediately above the frame, draw a horizontal 2-ray from grid column 0 through the cell immediately left of the frame's right vertical edge. Leave the right vertical's column and everything to its right unchanged. This ray extends all the way to the left grid boundary even when the frame itself is offset to the right.
4. Leave all other cells untouched. Repeat for every frame, including frames at different positions and heights.

## Evidence / checks
- Demo: 10x10 frame at rows 3–6, columns 2–5. Its interior/top gap became 2, and row 2 columns 0–4 became 2; 5s stayed intact.
- Solved test: 10x10 frames at rows 1–4, columns 1–4 and rows 7–9, columns 5–8. Interior zeros were filled with 2; rays were row 0 columns 0–3 and row 6 columns 0–7, respectively. Submission was confirmed correct.
- Infer each bbox/right-edge and above-row independently; do not assume a fixed frame size or position. For a frame touching the top border, there is no above-row ray to draw.
